page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs. It is equipped with a massive 168.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server includes 472 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a highly specialized performance profile. The server demonstrates top-tier single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2344.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, due to its single physical core configuration, multi-core performance is limited, as reflected in its weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2872.0 and poor multi-core stress-ng results. Memory performance is mixed; while the Passmark memory score is average, the large-block read-only memory bandwidth is poor at 21.09 GB/sec.

The FX8-2mds_v2 offers a distinct qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads requiring vast memory capacity without the need for high parallel processing power. By decoupling massive RAM allocation from high vCPU counts, users can avoid paying for unneeded compute resources. This makes the instance highly suitable for memory-intensive, single-threaded legacy applications, small in-memory databases, caching layers, and lightweight data processing tasks that require a large memory footprint but rely primarily on single-core execution speed.
